description: Blank sex is treated as unknown and its group is not reported.

a.request: Matching laboratory records to their patient on `ID` (lab records with no matching patient are dropped), compute for each patient (by ID and sex) the average prothrombin time (`PT`) and the average of `IGA` − `IGM` per record, ignoring missing values. Also compute the mean of that IGA−IGM average across all patients, and divide each patient's IGA−IGM average by this overall mean. Then break the patients down by sex, leaving out patients whose `SEX` is blank (an empty string), since their sex is unknown. For each sex, report the sex, the average of the patients' average PT, the average of their IGA−IGM averages, and the average of their ratios to the overall mean.
a.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT P.ID AS ID, P.SEX AS SEX, AVG(L.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(L.IGA - L.IGM) AS avg_diff FROM Laboratory L JOIN Patient P ON P.ID = L.ID GROUP BY P.ID, P.SEX), r AS (SELECT ID, SEX, avg_pt, avg_diff, avg_diff / (AVG(avg_diff) OVER ()) AS ratio FROM p) SELECT SEX, AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_pt, AVG(avg_diff) AS avg_iga_minus_igm, AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM r WHERE SEX <> '' GROUP BY SEX

b.request: Join Laboratory to Patient on ID (dropping unmatched lab records), compute each patient's (ID, sex) average PT and average IGA−IGM per record ignoring NULLs, divide each patient's average IGA−IGM by the mean of those per-patient averages across all patients to get a ratio, then group by sex and report the average PT, average IGA−IGM, and average ratio per sex, excluding patients whose sex is blank/empty (unknown) so that group is not reported
b.sql: WITH per_patient AS (SELECT p.ID AS ID, p.SEX AS SEX, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(l.IGA - l.IGM) AS avg_diff FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX), with_ratio AS (SELECT ID, SEX, avg_pt, avg_diff, avg_diff / (SELECT AVG(avg_diff) FROM per_patient) AS ratio FROM per_patient) SELECT SEX, AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_pt, AVG(avg_diff) AS avg_iga_minus_igm, AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM with_ratio WHERE SEX IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(SEX) <> '' GROUP BY SEX

c.request: Matching laboratory records to their patient on `ID` (lab records with no matching patient are dropped), work out each patient's (by ID and sex) average prothrombin time (`PT`) and average `IGA` − `IGM` difference per record, ignoring missing values. Also work out how each patient's IGA−IGM average compares to the mean across all patients, as their average divided by that mean. Then break this down by sex: for each sex, give the average PT, the average IGA−IGM difference, and the average ratio to the overall mean. Blank sex is treated as unknown and its group is not reported.
c.sql: WITH per_patient AS (SELECT p.ID AS ID, p.SEX AS SEX, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(l.IGA - l.IGM) AS avg_diff FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_diff) AS overall_mean FROM per_patient), ratios AS (SELECT pp.ID, pp.SEX, pp.avg_pt, pp.avg_diff, pp.avg_diff * 1.0 / o.overall_mean AS ratio FROM per_patient pp CROSS JOIN overall o) SELECT SEX, AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_pt, AVG(avg_diff) AS avg_iga_igm_diff, AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio_to_overall_mean FROM ratios WHERE SEX IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(SEX) <> '' GROUP BY SEX

d.request: Matching laboratory records to their patient on `ID` (lab records with no matching patient are dropped), work out each patient's (by ID and sex) average prothrombin time (`PT`) and average `IGA` − `IGM` difference per record, ignoring missing values. Also work out how each patient's IGA−IGM average compares to the mean across all patients, as their average divided by that mean. Then break this down by sex: for each sex, give the average PT, the average IGA−IGM difference, and the average ratio to the overall mean. Patients with a blank sex are treated as unknown, so that group should be excluded and not reported.
d.sql: WITH per_patient AS (SELECT p.ID AS ID, p.SEX AS SEX, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(l.IGA - l.IGM) AS avg_diff FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_diff) AS overall_mean FROM per_patient), ratios AS (SELECT pp.ID, pp.SEX, pp.avg_pt, pp.avg_diff, pp.avg_diff / o.overall_mean AS ratio FROM per_patient pp CROSS JOIN overall o) SELECT SEX, AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_pt, AVG(avg_diff) AS avg_iga_igm_diff, AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio_to_overall_mean FROM ratios WHERE SEX IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(SEX) <> '' GROUP BY SEX
